cells.tense: Right now you are standing in what someone else is feeling and keeping your own feet.
cells.ask: Offer this to someone today: stay with what they're feeling for two minutes longer than you'd like, and say nothing that fixes it. Notice when you want to step in, and don't.
cells.core:
You can stand near what someone else is feeling and keep your own feet. What they're going through lands in you as something you know, not something to pick up and carry home. That's the shape of what's working: you recognize what another person is going through, and you don't disappear into it. You stay someone while it happens.

It's a real balance and it's easier to lose than to keep. Press it and the feeling either stops coming in or it comes all the way in until there's no version of you left in the room. So the work is a small load taken on, kept small on purpose, and held without being swallowed. The recognition stays yours and theirs at once.
cells.sheetLine: You can feel with someone without becoming them.

cells.tense: You are already living inside other people's days before they've asked you into them.
cells.ask: Pick one person whose mood you're carrying. Say out loud, to yourself or them: 'this one isn't mine to fix,' and do nothing about their state for one hour.
cells.core:
You're taking on other people's states before they arrive. Somewhere up ahead, someone's bad day is already your bad day, and you're bracing for it — reading their face before they've made it, feeling their weight before they've set it down. The line between where they end and where you start goes thin.

That closeness is real, but it's being spent on something that hasn't landed yet. The connection you're trying to keep gets thinner each time you dissolve into it. What's called for isn't less care. It's letting one ending be an ending — one thing you've been holding for someone else finished, said out loud, and set down. Then you can feel with them from your own side again.

cells.tense: You stopped letting anyone in, and the distance is still running.
cells.ask: Tell one person one true thing about how your week actually went — not the summary version, the real one — and leave it there without adding anything to soften it.
cells.core:
You haven't let anything land in a while. People talk to you and you hear them, and there's a pane between you and them that stopped being noticeable. Conversations stay where they are — pleasant, functional, nothing getting through. It keeps you safe and it keeps you alone in the same room.

What would come back is the small adjustment that lets something in and lets something back out in the same motion — you sense where the other person is and you answer from there. The way back into that isn't forcing yourself to care. It's letting one honest thing come out of you, once, to someone, and noticing there's still ground underneath when you do.

cells.tense: You are already giving people something real, and you're describing it as nothing much.
cells.ask: Say 'I did that because I care' about one thing you did for someone this week and have been calling just being practical. One time, out loud, then stop.
cells.core:
People around you feel something from you — a steadiness, an attention, the sense that they aren't alone under your roof — and you'd say it's just being practical. That steadiness is a pattern you already run well. You notice what someone's carrying before they mention it, you adjust around it, you stay close without making it a scene. The care is arriving. You're the only one not receiving it.

Look at how it works in one moment when you're carrying something for another person and call it what it is instead of what it does. Not a feeling to declare. Just the plain fact of what you did and why. Your name belongs back on it.
